author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: “To be free, the French people had kings to fight. […]”
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858) — public domain (French)
context: Return presentation, Campo Formio in his pocket. Translated for Chronicle from the public-domain French; original below.
originalText: Le peuple français, pour être libre, avait les rois à combattre.

author: The Executive Directory
displayText: “Enclosed, Citizen General, a copy of the secret convention between the French Republic and the Emperor. […]”
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858) — public domain (French)
context: Incoming voice: secret convention with the Emperor, execute in Italy. Translated for Chronicle from the public-domain French; original below.
originalText: Vous trouverez ci-joint, Citoyen Général, une copie de la convention secrète conclue entre la République française et l'Empereur.

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: “I have just received your works. Your pen is a paintbrush. […]”
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858) — public domain (French)
context: Napoleon the reader: your pen is a paintbrush. Translated for Chronicle from the public-domain French; original below.
originalText: Je reçois à l'instant un exemplaire de vos ouvrages. Votre plume est un pinceau.

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: “The votes of the distinguished men of the Institut honor me. Before being their equal I shall long be their schoolboy. […]”
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858) — public domain (French)
context: Elected to the Institut: long their schoolboy first. Translated for Chronicle from the public-domain French; original below.
originalText: Le suffrage des hommes distingués qui composent l'Institut m'honore. Je sens bien qu'avant d'être leur égal je serai longtemps leur écolier.

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: “Months ago I sent two deputies to the Maniots. […]”
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858) — public domain (French)
context: Maniot deputies: Greece watched from Paris. Translated for Chronicle from the public-domain French; original below.
originalText: Il y a plusieurs mois que j'envoyai chez les Maniotes deux députés.

author: The Executive Directory
displayText: “The Executive Directory sees with liveliest indignation Rome's conduct. […]”
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858) — public domain (French)
context: Incoming voice: Duphot's murderers shall not go unpunished; Rome next. Translated for Chronicle from the public-domain French; original below.
originalText: Le Directoire exécutif n'a vu qu'avec la plus vive indignation la conduite de la cour de Rome.

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: “I received, my dear General, the letters you wrote me. The honor of taking Rome is reserved to you. […]”
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858) — public domain (French)
context: Midnight: the honor of taking Rome is reserved to you. Translated for Chronicle from the public-domain French; original below.
originalText: J'ai reçu, mon cher Général, les lettres que vous m'avez écrites. L'honneur de prendre Rome vous est réservé.

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: “Enclosed, Citizen Minister, the notes you asked of me. […]”
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858) — public domain (French)
context: Cisalpine notes: Mantua, Ferrara to be named. Translated for Chronicle from the public-domain French; original below.
originalText: Vous trouverez ci-joint, Citoyen Ministre, les notes que vous m'avez demandées.

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: “By the latest Levant letters, our commissioners offered French mediation to Ali, pasha of Janina. […]”
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858) — public domain (French)
context: Ali Pasha offered French mediation via Ionian agents. Translated for Chronicle from the public-domain French; original below.
originalText: Par les dernières lettres du Levant, nos commissaires ont offert la médiation de la République française à Ali, pacha de Janina.

author: Napoleon Bonaparte
displayText: “I received your letter announcing your departure for Rome. Arrive as fast as you can. […]”
archive: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier, Second Empire ed. (Paris, 1858) — public domain (French)
context: Hurry to Rome; Mainz army shown off to overawe the Emperor. Translated for Chronicle from the public-domain French; original below.
originalText: J'ai reçu votre lettre qui m'annonce votre départ pour Rome. Il faut arriver le plus vite que vous pourrez.
